title: Glycemic Variability After SASI Versus Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass
official: Comparison of Glycemic Variability After Bariatric Surgery With Single Anastomosis Sleeve Ileal Bypass (SASI) Versus Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring
summary: The GLUBARI trial is a prospective, randomized, single-center clinical study comparing two bariatric surgical procedures in adults with morbid obesity: Single Anastomosis Sleeve Ileal Bypass (SASI) and Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB). The main objective is to compare glycemic variability between the two procedures using continuous glucose monitoring. Participants will undergo continuous glucose monitoring for 7 days before surgery and again at 6 and 12 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes include hypoglycemic events, weight loss, resolution of obesity-related comorbidities, postoperative complications, gastroesophageal reflux, nutritional deficiencies, and quality of life. A total of 68 participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to SASI or RYGB and followed for 12 months after surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older and younger than 75 years.
* Morbid obesity with body mass index (BMI) between 35 and 55 kg/m².
* Pre-anesthetic assessment classified as ASA I-III.
* Signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Body mass index (BMI) \>55 kg/m².
* Previous major gastrointestinal surgery.
* Diseases that alter interstitial fluid volume and may affect glucose measurement accuracy, including severe acute or chronic renal failure, heart failure, or liver failure.
* Pathological gastroesophageal reflux disease with endoscopic involvement.
* Pre-anesthetic assessment not suitable for surgery or ASA IV.
* Pregnancy.
* Alcohol addiction.
* Active malignancy.
* Refusal to sign informed consent.
* Inability to comply with study instructions.'
